meta.purpose: Эталон кодов и заголовков книги «Klinik Psixiatriya». Единственный источник истины для шапки каждой страницы расстройства (XBT-11 · XBT-10 · DSM-5-TR), реестра abbreviatur.html и оглавления — на 4 языках.

pozuntu_vs_pozgunluq.evidence: MoH clinical protocols: pozuntu 562 vs pozğunluq 8 (98.6% pozuntu). XBT-10 AZ F-chapter: pozğunluq 544 vs pozuntu 1 (the reverse). ATU psychiatry lectures: pozuntu 35 vs pozğunluq 5.
pozuntu_vs_pozgunluq.explanation: Two registers exist. POZĞUNLUQ belongs to the older XBT-10 Azerbaijani volume — a literal translation from the Russian МКБ-10, with visible quality problems (typos such as 'həyəçan', 'içtimai', 'aqrofobiya', 'pozğunqluq', archaic 'pasient'). Every Ministry of Health clinical protocol from 2009 onward switched to POZUNTU, and the İSİM primary-care series even re-titles the ICD-10 chapter itself as 'F — Psixi pozuntular və davranış pozuntuları'. Note also that 'pozğunluq' carries a moral/deviance connotation in general Azerbaijani, which is a further reason the clinical literature moved away from it.
pozuntu_vs_pozgunluq.recommendation: POZUNTU throughout. This already matches the project's CLAUDE.md rule ('psixi pozuntu'). Cite XBT-10's pozğunluq forms only when quoting ICD-10 rubrics verbatim.

affektiv_vs_ahval.answer: BOTH — but they are not interchangeable: AFFEKTİV in disorder names, ƏHVAL for the mood state itself
affektiv_vs_ahval.evidence: MoH protocols: affektiv 51, əhval 54. XBT-10: affektiv 71, əhval 33. XBT-10 heading: 'Əhvali-ruhiyyə pozğunluqları (affektiv pozğunluq) (F30–F39)' and repeatedly 'Əhval pozğunluqları [affektiv pozğunluqlar]' — the Latin term is given as the technical equivalent in brackets.
affektiv_vs_ahval.explanation: The official disorder name is BİPOLYAR AFFEKTİV POZUNTU (title of the 2009 MoH protocol). 'Affektiv epizod' is the MoH 2021 term (6A80.x 'Affektiv epizodlar zamanı təşvişin nəzərəçarpan əlamətləri'). Meanwhile 'əhval' / 'əhval-ruhiyyə' is used for the mood state and for mood stabilisers ('əhval ruhiyyə stabilizatorları', MOH_SCH2021).
affektiv_vs_ahval.recommendation: Per the author's rule (keep the Latin/international term where it exists in AZ clinical usage): use AFFEKTİV in disorder names — 'Affektiv pozuntular', 'Bipolyar affektiv pozuntu', 'Affektiv epizod'. Use 'əhval' / 'əhval-ruhiyyə' for the mood state in descriptive prose. This mirrors the English→Russian shift (mood disorder → аффективные расстройства).

bodily_distress.answer: No attested Azerbaijani term — recommend BƏDƏN DİSSTRESİ POZUNTUSU
bodily_distress.evidence: ICD-11 6C20 Bodily distress disorder has no Azerbaijani rendering in any source reached. However DİSSTRESS is independently attested in official MoH protocols (9 occurrences, e.g. 'emosional disstress yaradır', MOH_ANX2013), so the Latin root is already naturalised in Azerbaijani clinical register.
bodily_distress.explanation: The ICD-10-era equivalent in XBT-10 AZ is 'F45 Somatoform pozğunluqlar' → modern MoH register 'Somatoform pozuntular' (13 occurrences in the corpus). The ICD-11 concept itself is new and untranslated.
bodily_distress.recommendation: Per the author's rule, keep the term: BƏDƏN DİSSTRESİ POZUNTUSU (compare Russian 'расстройство телесного дистресса'). Do not invent a descriptive translation such as 'bədən narahatlığı'. Flag it in the textbook as a new ICD-11 category, with 'somatoform pozuntular' given as the familiar ICD-10 predecessor.

icd11_azerbaijani_edition.answer: NO free Azerbaijani ICD-11 (XBT-11) exists online — confirmed
icd11_azerbaijani_edition.evidence: The WHO ICD-11 MMS browser (https://icd.who.int/browse/2025-01/mms/en) offers 14 languages: Arabic, Chinese, Czech, English, French, Kazakh, Latin, Portuguese, Russian, Slovak, Spanish, Swedish, Turkish, Uzbek. Azerbaijani is NOT among them. No AZ ICD-11 volume was found on isim.az, sehiyye.gov.az, or psychiatry.az.
icd11_azerbaijani_edition.important_nuance: HOWEVER — Azerbaijani ICD-11 disorder names DO exist officially, embedded inside the Ministry of Health's 2021 clinical protocols. The Depression 2021, Schizophrenia 2021, Dementia 2021 and PTSD 2021 protocols are all built on ICD-11 codes with Azerbaijani names (6A20 Şizofreniya, 6A71 Rekurrent depressiv pozuntu, 6A73 Qarışıq depressiv və təşviş pozuntusu, 6B42 Uzanmış hüzn pozuntusu, 6D80 Alsheymer xəstəliyi nəticəsində demensiya, 6D86.2 Demensiya zamanı təşviş simptomları). These are the closest thing to an official XBT-11 AZ vocabulary that exists, and they are the single most valuable source for this textbook.
icd11_azerbaijani_edition.printed_edition_claim: Could not confirm or refute a printed Azerbaijani ICD-11 by the İsmayılov family. Prof. Nadir İsmayılov chairs AzPA and F.İsmayılov (Psixi Sağlamlıq Mərkəzi director) authored several MoH protocols, so the family is plausibly involved — but no such publication is listed on psychiatry.az or isim.az. I have no evidence either way; treat the printed edition as unverified.

az_anxiety_verdict.confidence: high — settled by official Ministry of Health clinical protocols
az_anxiety_verdict.summary: In Azerbaijani PSYCHIATRIC CLINICAL sources the accepted term for 'anxiety' is TƏŞVİŞ. The Ministry of Health's dedicated anxiety protocol is literally titled 'TƏŞVİŞ POZUNTULARININ DİAQNOSTİKA VƏ MÜALİCƏSİ ÜZRƏ KLİNİK PROTOKOL' (Bakı 2013), and the newest ICD-11-aligned MoH protocols (Depression 2021, Dementia 2021) keep TƏŞVİŞ. NARAHATLIQ is not the disorder term — in the same protocols it means 'worry / unease' (the GAD worry component). HƏYƏCAN is the older ICD-10-volume calque, still used descriptively for autonomic arousal. ANKSİYETE does not occur in any Azerbaijani official source (it is Turkish).
